result.heading: Endorsement HO-2026-01 — Water Backup and Sump Discharge or Overflow
result.text:
**Attaches to:** HO-3-2026 base form
**Effective:** 01 March 2026
**Premium:** $68 annual, or $112 annual at the $25,000 limit option

---

result.heading: Conditions
result.text:
Coverage under this endorsement applies **only if**:

- the sump pump and any related equipment were in **proper working order** at the time of
  loss; and
- for dwellings with a finished basement, a **battery backup sump system or water alarm**
  is installed, where the dwelling was built or the basement finished after 01 January 2020.

Where the required backup system is absent, the limit is reduced to **$2,500** rather than
being voided entirely.

result.heading: My basement flooded after heavy rain. Am I covered?
result.text:
It depends on how the water got in. If water **backed up through a drain or sewer**, or a
**sump pump overflowed**, and you have endorsement HO-2026-01, you are covered up to
$10,000 (or $25,000 if you chose the higher limit) with a $500 deductible. If **surface
water flowed in** from outside — over the ground, through a window well, or from a river or
storm surge — that is **flood**, and flood is not covered by any endorsement in this pack.
Flood cover must be bought separately.

result.heading: Exclusions specific to this endorsement
What this endorsement does
result.text:
Exclusion 3 of the base form excludes water which backs up through sewers or drains. This
endorsement **deletes that portion of the exclusion** and adds the coverage described
below. All other terms of exclusion 3 — including flood, surface water and overflow of a
body of water — remain fully excluded and are **not** restored by this endorsement.

result.heading: Deductible
result.text:
A **separate deductible of $500** applies to each water backup occurrence. This deductible
applies **instead of**, not in addition to, the base all-perils deductible of $1,000.

result.heading: 3. Deductible application
result.text:
The deductible is applied **once per occurrence**, not once per coverage. Where an
endorsement carries its own deductible, that deductible replaces the base deductible for
the portion of the loss falling under the endorsement:

- Water backup (HO-2026-01): **$500**, replacing the base $1,000
- Service line (HO-2026-02): **$500**, replacing the base $1,000
- Equipment breakdown (HO-2026-03): **$500**, replacing the base $1,000
- Scheduled property (HO-2026-04): **no deductible**
- Identity fraud (HO-2026-07): **$250**

Where a single occurrence triggers both a base-form loss and an endorsement loss, apply the
**base deductible once to the base-form portion** and the endorsement deductible once to
the endorsement portion. Do not apply the base deductible to the endorsement portion as
well.

result.heading: SECTION 4 - Deductible
result.text:
A $100 deductible applies per warranty claim under this endorsement, separate from and in
addition to any deductible applying to the underlying water damage claim, if any.

result.heading: Claim handling note
result.text:
Water backup claims are assigned to the **Property — Water team** and carry a target
first-contact time of **one business day** from First Notice of Loss. A moisture-mapping
inspection is required before any payment above **$5,000**.

result.heading: Definition of breakdown
result.text:
**Breakdown** means the sudden and accidental physical damage to covered equipment that
requires its repair or replacement, arising from:

- mechanical breakdown, including rupture or bursting caused by centrifugal force
- artificially generated electrical current, including electrical arcing
- explosion of steam boilers, steam pipes or steam engines
- loss or damage to hot water heating systems from freezing
- **power surge originating off the residence premises**, including surge from a utility
  fault or a lightning strike to the grid

Breakdown does **not** mean wear and tear on its own, gradual deterioration, rust,
corrosion, or a defect that has caused no sudden physical damage.

result.text:
